title: Monolith to Microservices
subtitle: Split by team pain, not by fashion
motto: Start with a monolith, and extract a service only when you can name the pain
keyInsight: Splitting into services trades coordination loss for a platform tax, so it only pays once the team is large enough for the coordination loss to dominate.

decisions.title: Model the team, not the servers
decisions.description: The sim counts productive engineers, because the note's argument is about people: coordination loss against platform overhead.
decisions.alternatives: A server-capacity model would miss that the main cost of splitting too early is engineering time, not machines.

decisions.title: Put a modular monolith between the two extremes
decisions.description: A modular monolith halves coordination loss with no new infrastructure, showing that the choice is not monolith versus microservices.
decisions.alternatives: Comparing only a monolith and full microservices would make it look like a leap that must be taken all at once.
